spec_features.spec_quote: Cap agent loop at 30 turns per task.
spec_features.evidence: experiment_config.py:13 'MAX_TURNS = 30'. In agent_loop.py:67 run(max_turns=MAX_TURNS) and the loop at agent_loop.py:91 'for turn_num in range(1, max_turns + 1):' is bounded by max_turns, so the loop terminates at 30 turns. Additionally _should_stop at agent_loop.py:357 'if turn_num >= MAX_TURNS: return True' breaks early (redundant with range bound). max_turns is threaded through harness (experiment_harness.py:181 'turns, transcript = loop.run(max_turns=self.max_turns)') and CLI default 30 (main.py --max-turns default=30). MockAgentLoop also loops range(1, max_turns+1) at agent_loop.py:401. The cap is genuinely enforced and bounds execution.
spec_features.notes: Default is 30 and the for-loop's range hard-bounds the number of agent turns regardless of the _should_stop check. The redundant _should_stop 'i give up' branch checks system feedback text (not agent response) so that branch is effectively dead, but the turn cap itself is real via the range bound.

spec_features.feature_name: early termination based on partial results
spec_features.spec_quote: Can analyze partial results to decide whether to continue or terminate early.
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:229) describing a hypothetical benefit of incremental logging. The only related code is incremental logging: experiment_harness.py:215 'if len(self.experiment_log) % 5 == 0: self._save_experiment_log()' which just writes results to experiment_log.jsonl. There is NO code path that reads partial results and decides to stop the experiment. The main loop run_complete_experiment (experiment_harness.py:108-123) iterates over every model x task unconditionally with no break/terminate based on accumulated scores. grep for 'terminate'/'early' finds only DESIGN.md and an unrelated analysis comparison in advanced_analysis.py. No enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Logging-every-5-runs is implemented, but the early-stopping/terminate decision it supposedly enables is never coded; the experiment always runs to completion.
